title: When Forces Disagree: A Data-Free Fast Uncertainty Estimate for Direct-Force Pre-trained Neural Network Potentials
experiments_summary: The study introduces and validates the 'Force Delta' (U_Δ) uncertainty metric, defined as the RMS difference between conservative forces (derived via automatic differentiation of predicted energy) and non-conservative forces (predicted directly by a separate output head) for neural network interatomic potentials. Experiments were conducted as follows: (1) Baseline evaluation on in-distribution structures: For 10 material systems, equilibrium configurations were evaluated using 15 pre-trained models (from the EquiformerV2 and Orb model families). The average Force Delta and average true error (RMS difference between directly predicted forces and DFT reference forces) were computed per system, and their monotonic association was assessed using Spearman's rank correlation. (2) Benchmark against ensemble-based UQ: The Force Delta from individual models was compared against ensemble variance computed from ad-hoc collections of pre-trained models (10 EquiformerV2 models and 5 Orb models), using Spearman's rank correlation as the performance criterion, conducted separately within each model family due to differing DFT training setups. (3) Adversarial attack generation of OOD structures: Starting from equilibrium structures, atomic positions were iteratively perturbed using a composite gradient that simultaneously maximized U_Δ and minimized predicted potential energy, with separate learning rates for each objective, to generate physically plausible but high-uncertainty out-of-distribution configurations. (4) Evaluation on OOD structures: The Force Delta was computed for both standard and adversarially generated structures for the Orb potential across all 10 systems, and the correlation between U_Δ and true error was assessed via parity plots and Spearman's rank correlation. (5) Generalization to EquiformerV2: The same analysis (equilibrium and adversarial OOD) was repeated for EquiformerV2 across six material systems to assess cross-architecture generality of the metric.
